claims.claim: The 2005 UEFA Champions League final was contested between Milan of Italy and Liverpool of England at the Atatürk Olympic Stadium in Istanbul on 25 May 2005.
claims.excerpt: The showpiece event was contested between Milan of Italy and Liverpool of England at the Atatürk Olympic Stadium in Istanbul on 25 May 2005.
claims.context: The final match of the 2004-05 UEFA Champions League took place in Istanbul.

claims.claim: Liverpool reached the final by finishing second in their group behind Monaco and beating Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus, and Chelsea.
claims.excerpt: Liverpool finished second in their group behind 2004 runners-up Monaco and subsequently beat Bayer Leverkusen, Juventus and Chelsea to progress to the final.
claims.context: Liverpool's path to the 2005 Champions League final involved navigating the group stage and knockout rounds.

claims.claim: Milan won their group ahead of Barcelona and faced Manchester United, Inter Milan, and PSV Eindhoven before reaching the final.
claims.excerpt: Milan won their group ahead of Barcelona and faced Manchester United, Inter Milan and PSV Eindhoven before reaching the final.
claims.context: Milan's progression to the 2005 Champions League final included matches against several major European clubs.

claims.claim: Prior to the game, Milan were assured of entering the Champions League the following season after finishing second in Serie A.
claims.excerpt: Prior to the game, Milan were assured of entering the Champions League the following season after finishing second in Serie A.
claims.context: Milan had already secured their qualification for the next iteration of the tournament through their domestic league finish.

claims.claim: Liverpool failed to finish in the top four in the Premier League and had to win the final to enter the competition the following season.
claims.excerpt: Liverpool meanwhile had failed to finish in the top four in the Premier League, and had to win the final to enter the competition the following season.
claims.context: Liverpool's qualification for the subsequent Champions League season depended heavily on the outcome of the final.

claims.claim: Milan were regarded as favourites and their team included many players who had experienced success in the competition.
claims.excerpt: Milan were regarded as favourites and their team included many players who had experienced success in the competition.
claims.context: Milan entered the match carrying expectations as the stronger side with experienced winners in their squad.

claims.claim: Liverpool had been considered underdogs throughout the competition, but had beaten more favoured opposition to reach the final.
claims.excerpt: Liverpool had been considered underdogs throughout the competition, but had beaten more favoured opposition, including Juventus and Chelsea, to reach the final.
claims.context: Liverpool's journey to the final was marked by overcoming teams that were favored against them.

claims.claim: Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger felt Liverpool would win the match because Milan looked jaded physically and mentally by losing the Serie A title.
claims.excerpt: Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger felt Liverpool would win the match: "I fancy Liverpool as Milan look jaded physically and certainly mentally, by losing the [Serie A] title, I think they have never had a better chance than now to beat Milan."
claims.context: External opinions on the matchup included Arsène Wenger's assessment of Milan's condition.
